findings.motion: SB 10 - Culp - 3rd Reading: Bill Passed (roll call 340)
findings.note: IN House, SB 10 - Culp - 3rd Reading: Bill Passed (roll call 340), 2025-04-01: nay (tally 66–26); census gate: none.

findings.passage: At a time when voter participation is already appalling low, SB 10 creates yet another unnecessary hurdle for Hoosier voters.
findings.note: Statement issued in her name by the House caucus after she voted against SB 10 in the House Elections and Apportionment Committee. The release dates from the page's 2025-03-26 stamp. It calls the bill an added hurdle for voters.
subjects: student ID as proof of identity

findings.passage: Denying them the ability to vote with the IDs they use every day would be a step backward for our democracy.
findings.note: Same release. Speaks about college students and the IDs they use daily (student IDs) as proof of identity to vote.
subjects: student ID as proof of identity

findings.passage: We should be making it easier, not harder, for eligible voters to participate in our elections, and I will continue to fight for the rights of college students and all Hoosiers to have their voices heard.
findings.note: Same release; her closing statement on SB 10.

findings.motion: Committee amendment to SB 10: remove the language that bars a document issued by an educational institution from counting as proof of identification
findings.note: Per the caucus release, in the House Elections and Apportionment Committee she proposed this amendment and it was voted down by a party line vote. She also voted against SB 10 in that committee (final votes already on file).
subjects: student ID as proof of identity

findings.note: Blog post (Doug Masson; secondary source, official bill page unreachable) dated 2007-01-09 says Sen. Errington filed SB 182, 'Voter identification', creating alternate acceptable ways to prove identity to vote: ID from the state, the U.S. or an Indiana college; a utility bill, bank statement, paycheck or government document with name and address; an out-of-state license or ID; and an affidavit from two precinct officers of different major parties or the voter's own sworn affidavit.

findings.note: Blog post (Doug Masson; secondary source, official bill page unreachable) dated 2008-12-31 says Senator Errington introduced SB 5, which expands the permissible forms of voter identification: a utility bill, bank statement, paycheck or government check with name and address; an out-of-state driver's license or state ID; and a two-officer affidavit.
